summary: Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his BA at Sir C. R. Reddy College, MA and PhD at Andhra University, and diploma at Osmania University, later holding posts at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, and Emory.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008), president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018), and on the boards of Indologica Taurinensia and the Wider Association of Vedic Studies.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research posts at St Edmund's College and St Hilda's College, taught at King's College London, and became George A. Saden Professor at Yale University in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was an Indologist and historian who studied at Dean Close School and Merton College. From circa 1945 to 1949, he served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India.

Vesna A. Wallace works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. After completing her doctoral dissertation at UC Berkeley, she held posts at Oxford as Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies and at UC Santa Barbara as Distinguished University Professor.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA at Yale University and a PhD at SOAS University of London. In 1984, he became Raoul Wallenberg Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a scholar of Tibetology who completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago. He was Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia (~2003) and founded the Dalai Lama Center in 2005.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Temple University in 2004. In 2007, he was attested as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard (PhD ~1976), then taught as an assistant professor at Harvard before becoming a professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Henry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Douai, the University of Lille, and École Centrale de Lille before becoming professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner was a scholar of religion who studied at University College London and the University of Manchester. He held appointments at the Rhodes-Livingstone Institute, University of Manchester, Cornell University, University of Chicago (1968–1977), and University of Virginia (1977).

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at St. Xavier's, Newnham College, and Cambridge (PhD). She served at the Smithsonian Institution and joined Columbia University, becoming the Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya at Allahabad University. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1992–1994).
Vijayalakshmi Mani is an Indology and history scholar who, as attested in 2026, pursued PhD studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen. He taught at Borgerdydskolen and held academic posts at Copenhagen, serving as professor from 1887 to 1913, and later as President of the Royal Danish Academy.

Vinay Lal is a scholar of history and Indology who studied at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1980 to 1982. In circa 1993, he became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA.

Vincenc Lesný was an Indologist who studied at Charles University (~1903–1907) under Moriz Winternitz and Josef Zubatý. He subsequently held a faculty post at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts from circa 1924 to 1953.

Vincent Arthur Smith was an Indologist and historian who earned a doctorate from Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1871 to 1900, at St John's College, and as Curator at Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Lucia Dolce, attended Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono universities, and earned his MA and PhD at Leiden University, where he was attested as a research fellow in 2012.
